correctness.rationale: For a signed m-vertex face on S, the Euclidean foot has x_i=b_i+s_i(1−Σ_{j∈S}s_j b_j)/m on S and zero elsewhere. Positivity of the i-th signed barycentric coordinate for all sign choices is equivalent to (m−1)|b_i|+Σ_{j∈S∖{i}}|b_j|<1, because the signs at i and at the other coordinates can be chosen independently. The full-support inequalities dominate every smaller support and imply interior membership, giving exactly the stated strict kernel. Its closure is the corresponding weak ball by radial scaling. Each of the d·2^d given normals uniquely supports a facet at a point of the chosen signs with unique absolute maximum at its distinguished index. Signed order chambers give all possible vertices s/(d−2+|supp s|); the listed candidates are extreme because the active-normal differences generate d−1 directions perpendicular to the point (off-support flips and on-support changes of distinguished index), and one active normal supplies the last direction. The origin is interior. The order-difference coordinates give a simplex with volume 1/[d!∏_{j=1}^d(d−2+j)]; counting all 2^d d! chambers gives the volume and fraction. The central-binomial asymptotic at d−1 recovers 4√(πd)/4^d. At d=4 the volume is 2/45 and the fraction is 1/15.
residual_risks: The new computation is only a bounded check in dimension four. The general result follows from the proof, not a finite sample. The problem uses the stated regular Euclidean realization, not arbitrary affine cross-polytopes.

evidence: The generic orthogonal kernel and face active regions are already defined. Pavlík's kernel-to-tiling equivalence is dimension three; the companion's cross-polytope supplies a different interval realization, with 3^d+1 vertices.

The OWL atomic formulation gives the convex hull of signed permutations of constant-prefix vectors with value 1/(w₁+…+w_k), i.e. 1/(d−2+k) for the weights here. This is real broader coverage of the hull representation, not a prior all-face kernel theorem. With repeated weights minimality does not follow from the general strict-decrease criterion alone.

The same-day Resultary a129853e89b6 computes axial three-dimensional octahedron kernels and includes the regular d=3 case; 4c637740730d computes parallelotope kernels using the Gram matrix, for a different polytope class.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader norm theorem supplies the ball form once weights are specified, but not the projection-based derivation of those weights. Neither the distinct d=3 axial family nor the parallelotope result covers regular higher-dimensional cross-polytopes.

value.rationale: The natural all-face admissibility test ranges over exponentially many faces. In the original regular Euclidean embedding it reduces to two norms, and the exact volume determines how rare simultaneous relative-interior feet are for uniform anchors in high dimension. The point is this geometric identification and the associated probability, not a renaming of a known mixed-norm ball.
residual_risks: No higher-dimensional bipolar tiling implication or arbitrary affine kernel computation follows from this review.
